plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, PLTU, MUU, MSFU) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration.
Hold broad index (SPY, QQQ) and income (QQQI).
Focus on capital preservation with tight stops.
Maintain a significant cash buffer for safety.
This plan prioritizes low drawdown over high returns.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for ~1.5% monthly growth with a strong focus on capital preservation. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also capped upside potential. Leverage is minimized.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, PLTU, MUU, MSFU) to low single digits.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration.
Buy XLV as a defensive sector addition.
Maintain a blend of broad index, quality tech, and some leverage.
Keep a moderate cash buffer of around 10%.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth opportunities.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5% monthly growth with a risk-first approach. It reduces concentration and leverage while adding some diversification. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, METU, PLTU, MUU, MSFU) up to 6% each.
Trim QQQI to 15% to free up capital for growth.
Buy XLV as a high-scoring scanner setup.
Concentrate positions in high-conviction, leveraged names.
Maintain a small cash buffer of around 5%.
This plan aims for aggressive growth but carries significant risk and potential for large drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% monthly growth by leaning into leverage and concentration. Expect higher potential returns but also significantly larger drawdowns and the risk of rapid losses, especially with leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names (SOXL, SPAL, METU, PLTU, MUU, MSFU, SMH, CRWD, SNOW, SMCI).
Increase QQQI to 30% for income generation.
Trim SPY to 20% to make room for income focus.
Prioritize steady monthly distributions over growth.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
This plan focuses on capital preservation and reliable income, accepting lower growth potential.
income.read: This income-focused plan targets ~1% monthly distributions, prioritizing stability and cash flow. While aiming for low drawdowns, NAV can still decline in market downturns. Distributions are not guaranteed and can vary.
